zerobrew

English · 中文

zerobrew brings uv-style architecture to Homebrew packages on macOS and Linux.

## Install ```bash curl -fsSL https://zerobrew.rs/install | bash ``` The installer updates your shell config. After it finishes, restart your terminal or run the `source` command it prints. Or via Homebrew: ```bash brew install lucasgelfond/zerobrew/zerobrew ``` ## Update zerobrew If you used the standalone installer, rerun it: ```bash curl -fsSL https://zerobrew.rs/install | bash zb --version ``` If you installed with Homebrew: ```bash brew update && brew upgrade zerobrew ``` ## Quick start ```bash zb install jq # install one package zb install wget git # install multiple zb bundle # install from Brewfile zb bundle install -f myfile # install from custom file zb bundle dump # export installed packages to Brewfile zb bundle dump -f out --force # dump to custom file (overwrite) zb uninstall jq # uninstall one package zb outdated # list packages with newer versions zb upgrade # upgrade all outdated packages zb upgrade jq wget # upgrade specific packages zb reset # uninstall everything zb gc # garbage collect unused store entries zbx jq --version # run without linking ``` ## Performance snapshot
| Package | Homebrew | ZB (cold) | ZB (warm) | Cold Speedup | Warm Speedup | |---------|----------|-----------|-----------|--------------|--------------| | **Overall (top 100)** | 452s | 226s | 59s | **2.0x** | **7.6x** | | ffmpeg | 3034ms | 3481ms | 688ms | 0.9x | 4.4x | | libsodium | 2353ms | 392ms | 130ms | 6.0x | 18.1x | | sqlite | 2876ms | 625ms | 159ms | 4.6x | 18.1x | | tesseract | 18950ms | 5536ms | 643ms | 3.4x | 29.5x |
## Relationship with Homebrew zerobrew is more of a performance-optimized client for the Homebrew ecosystem. We rely on: - Homebrew's formula definitions (homebrew-core) - Homebrew's pre-built bottles when available - Homebrew's package metadata and infrastructure Our innovations focus on: - Content-addressable storage for deduplication - APFS clonefiles for zero-overhead copying - Source build fallback using Homebrew's Ruby DSL zerobrew is experimental. We recommend running it alongside Homebrew rather than as a replacement, and do _not_ recommend purging homebrew and replacing it with zerobrew unless you are absolutely sure about the implications of doing so. ## Project status
- **Status:** Experimental, but already useful for many common Homebrew formulas. - **Feedback:** If you hit incompatibilities, please open an issue or PR. - **License:** Dual-licensed under [Apache 2.0](./LICENSE-APACHE.md) OR [MIT](./LICENSE-MIT.md), at your choice.
readmeHtml:
zerobrew

English · 中文

zerobrew brings uv-style architecture to Homebrew packages on macOS and Linux.

Install

curl -fsSL https://zerobrew.rs/install | bash

The installer updates your shell config. After it finishes, restart your terminal or run the source command it prints.

Or via Homebrew:

brew install lucasgelfond/zerobrew/zerobrew

Update zerobrew

If you used the standalone installer, rerun it:

curl -fsSL https://zerobrew.rs/install | bash
zb --version

If you installed with Homebrew:

brew update && brew upgrade zerobrew

Quick start

zb install jq                   # install one package
zb install wget git             # install multiple
zb bundle                       # install from Brewfile
zb bundle install -f myfile     # install from custom file
zb bundle dump                  # export installed packages to Brewfile
zb bundle dump -f out --force   # dump to custom file (overwrite)
zb uninstall jq                 # uninstall one package
zb outdated                     # list packages with newer versions
zb upgrade                      # upgrade all outdated packages
zb upgrade jq wget              # upgrade specific packages
zb reset                        # uninstall everything
zb gc                           # garbage collect unused store entries
zbx jq --version                # run without linking

Performance snapshot

Package Homebrew ZB (cold) ZB (warm) Cold Speedup Warm Speedup
Overall (top 100) 452s 226s 59s 2.0x 7.6x
ffmpeg 3034ms 3481ms 688ms 0.9x 4.4x
libsodium 2353ms 392ms 130ms 6.0x 18.1x
sqlite 2876ms 625ms 159ms 4.6x 18.1x
tesseract 18950ms 5536ms 643ms 3.4x 29.5x

Relationship with Homebrew

zerobrew is more of a performance-optimized client for the Homebrew ecosystem. We rely on:

  • Homebrew's formula definitions (homebrew-core)
  • Homebrew's pre-built bottles when available
  • Homebrew's package metadata and infrastructure

Our innovations focus on:

  • Content-addressable storage for deduplication
  • APFS clonefiles for zero-overhead copying
  • Source build fallback using Homebrew's Ruby DSL

zerobrew is experimental. We recommend running it alongside Homebrew rather than as a replacement, and do not recommend purging homebrew and replacing it with zerobrew unless you are absolutely sure about the implications of doing so.

Project status

  • Status: Experimental, but already useful for many common Homebrew formulas.
  • Feedback: If you hit incompatibilities, please open an issue or PR.
  • License: Dual-licensed under Apache 2.0 OR MIT, at your choice.

releases.name: v0.3.2
releases.body:
## What's Changed
* fix(zb_io): skip libexec/ for Python virtualenv kegs by @pmnmq in https://github.com/lucasgelfond/zerobrew/pull/383
* Fix/shim resource patch checksum verification by @cachebag in https://github.com/lucasgelfond/zerobrew/pull/388

#388 includes a fix for CVE-2026-53970: verify SHA-256 for resource and URL patch downloads in the build shim before extract/apply. Reported via VulnCheck coordinated disclosure (Khushali Dalal). 

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/lucasgelfond/zerobrew/compare/v0.3.1...v0.3.2

releases.name: v0.3.0
releases.body:
yo! this release includes two major new commands: `zb doctor` for diagnosing and repairing local state, and `zb upgrade` for upgrading installed packages. It also improves Linux bottle handling, Python package linking, migration behavior, formula alias resolution, CLI help text, and release stability.

Apologies for the delay and recent period of inactivity. Thanks for sticking with the project while we got this release together.

## What's Changed
* feat(site): v2 aka just the homepage by @maria-rcks in https://github.com/lucasgelfond/zerobrew/pull/309
* fix(zb_io, zb_cli): validate root/prefix paths before passing to sudo by @cachebag in https://github.com/lucasgelfond/zerobrew/pull/311
* refactor(zb_io): split monolothic install functionality into submodules by @cachebag in https://github.com/lucasgelfond/zerobrew/pull/312
* refactor(zb_io): split monolothic download functionality into submodules by @cachebag in https://github.com/lucasgelfond/zerobrew/pull/313
* feat(zb): `zb doctor` + `--repair` for state diagnosis and repair by @cachebag in https://github.com/lucasgelfond/zerobrew/pull/314
* docs: add Chinese translation (README.zh.md) by @JasonYeYuhe in https://git

releases.name: v0.2.0
releases.body:
hi there! 

**zerobrew v0.2.0** is a fairly large update focused on usability, stability, and better internal architecture.

this release introduces several new CLI commands, including `zb update` and `zb outdated`, along with batch processing for `zb migrate`. output handling has also been expanded with `--quiet`, `--verbose`, and `--json` modes, backed by a new tracing-based logging system (thanks to @maria-rcks). the UI layer is now configurable, allowing themes and writer-based output customization.

there are also a number of quality-of-life improvements. missing package errors now provide fuzzy formula suggestions, API requests can be cached locally, and the API endpoint can be overridden using `ZEROBREW_API_URL`.

internally, this release also improves reliability and performance. the installer now uses a global lock to prevent concurrent install corruption, SQLite schema versioning has been added with proper migrations, downloads are more memory efficient, and several edge cases around macOS bottles, Mach-O patching, and Linux linking have been addressed.

soon, we plan to make a more targeted approach towards our x86/intel support (both CI and the code). see #286

aiSummary.oneLiner: An experimental, dramatically faster alternative architecture for Homebrew packages on macOS and Linux.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: Zerobrew is an experimental package manager that brings a high-performance, uv-style architecture to the massive ecosystem of Homebrew packages across macOS and Linux. Built in Rust, it aims to be 5-20x faster than traditional Homebrew by fundamentally rethinking how packages are resolved, downloaded, and linked on the system. The project leverages advanced techniques like content-addressable storage for deduplication and APFS clonefiles for zero-overhead copying. It is designed to act as a seamless, high-speed client that interacts directly with existing Homebrew formulas and bottles, requiring no ecosystem rewrites. It serves as a drop-in solution designed to eliminate the long wait times traditionally associated with bootstrapping or updating developer environments.
keyFeatures: High-performance architecture: Implements a uv-style resolution and installation engine to achieve speeds 5-20x faster than traditional Homebrew.
Zero-overhead linking: Leverages APFS clonefiles and content-addressable storage to instantly copy and link packages without duplicating data.
Rust-based implementation: Built entirely in Rust to ensure memory safety, rapid execution, and highly parallelized network and disk operations.
Homebrew ecosystem compatibility: Designed to seamlessly utilize existing Homebrew formulas and pre-built bottles without requiring ecosystem changes.
Cross-platform support: Provides rapid package management capabilities for both macOS and Linux environments.

useCases.title: Rapid environment bootstrapping
useCases.description: Drastically reducing the time it takes developers to set up a new machine or provision a fresh continuous integration environment.

useCases.title: Fast package updates
useCases.description: Allowing system administrators to quickly update their daily drivers and CLI tools without waiting through typical Homebrew resolution delays.

useCases.title: CI/CD pipeline optimization
useCases.description: Replacing standard Homebrew commands in automated workflows with Zerobrew to significantly cut down build times and compute costs.

useCases.title: Seamless performance transition
useCases.description: Providing users with massive performance gains while retaining full access to the massive catalog of formulas they already rely on.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: Zerobrew is built for software developers, system administrators, and DevOps engineers frustrated by the speed of traditional package managers who want a hyper-fast alternative for macOS or Linux. Users are expected to have a basic understanding of the relevant underlying technologies.
